narrative:
The model determined that you have a 34% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three factors weighed most heavily in this decision. Your credit history had the strongest influence and pushed the outcome toward approval. Having a record marked as "critical or other credits" is relatively common among approved applicants (about one in three), so this actually worked in your favor. However, two other aspects pulled the prediction in the opposite direction with enough force to outweigh that positive signal.

The status of your checking account was the second most important factor. Your balance in the 0-200 DM range is less favorable than the "no checking account" situation that most approved borrowers have. This increased the perceived risk. The loan amount you requested was the third key driver. At 8,386 DM, your request is substantially higher than the average of roughly 3,020 DM seen among those who were approved, which further raised the model's concern about your ability to repay.

Taken together, the larger requested amount and your checking-account status created more doubt than your solid credit history could overcome. 

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a smaller loan amount and wait until your checking-account balance is more robust. This combination would likely produce a stronger application. (218 words)
